page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9a.xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. Compute capacity is supplied by 4 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9T25 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. Dedicated CPU core allocation ensures predictable execution without resource contention from neighboring virtual machines.

The server provides 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 core-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with no bundled local storage, requiring the use of network-attached block volumes for persistent filesystems. Network interface capabilities include a baseline throughput of 4 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned.

The architecture omits GPU accelerators and local NVMe storage, directing its cost profile toward high memory capacity rather than specialized graphics acceleration or high-speed ephemeral disk I/O. This hardware profile suits memory-sensitive tasks, including in-memory caching tiers, relational database engines, backend enterprise services, and data transformation pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9a.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server powered by KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs driven by an AMD EPYC 9T25 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. Equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers an elevated allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU, suiting memory-bound execution contexts. The instance includes 4 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and operates without bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators such as GPUs. Because it lacks onboard disk storage, data persistence depends on network-attached storage options. With its dedicated compute allocation, the instance avoids multi-tenant CPU throttling. The ecs.r9a.xlarge is structured for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory caches, database servers, intermediate data processing, and enterprise backend applications.
